name: The Depression sell-off
note: The market collapse was followed by banking panics. The wider depression cannot be reduced to one stock-market event.

name: A second severe decline
note: A separate local decline during the longer recovery from 1929. Its peak is local, not an all-time high.

name: The 1962 sell-off
note: An earlier comparison with valuation data but no modern VIX, curve-spread, or financial-stress series.

name: The 1966 decline
note: Compare the shape and duration of this local decline with later periods. Modern signal coverage is absent.

name: The late-sixties unwind
note: A local price peak and trough from a period of rising inflation. Available indicators are limited.

name: Inflation and the oil shock
note: The 1973 oil embargo occurred during the broader Great Inflation. The price series measures the decline, not its causal decomposition.

name: The tightening-era decline
note: A comparison from the end of the Great Inflation. Curve coverage begins only in 1982, near the end of this window.

name: Black Monday and its aftermath
note: A fast market break. Monthly-average prices smooth the daily shock, so these measurements differ from one-day crash figures.

name: The 1990 decline
note: The first catalogue episode with VIX coverage. The financial-stress series is not yet available.

name: The Russia / LTCM period
note: A financial-market disruption during the Great Moderation, useful for comparing short-lived stress with deeper declines.

name: The dot-com unwind
note: Compare valuation pressure before the peak with volatility and financial stress during the decline.

name: The global financial crisis
note: Mortgage losses, funding pressure, and a wider economic contraction developed over time. Compare which indicators moved early and which reacted.

name: The 2011 correction
note: A smaller local decline. Including corrections prevents the catalogue from containing only spectacular crashes.

name: The 2015–16 correction
note: A local correction for comparison with major crises. Its recovery is measured against its selected local peak.

name: The late-2018 correction
note: Another smaller decline for comparison. Monthly averages soften the depth of the late-year fall.

name: The pandemic shock
note: A sudden shock with rapid policy intervention. Monthly averages can miss much of the short daily drawdown.

name: The inflation / rates repricing
note: Monetary tightening and rising long-term yields coincided with weaker equity prices. The measurement does not attribute the decline to a single cause.
